question: Which Linux notification backend contract should OpenClaw support for the core headless node-host `system.notify` command?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the backend choice affects dependencies, invocation security, headless behavior, and support expectations across Linux desktop environments.

options.title: Bounded notify-send backend
options.body: Implement `notify-send` first with argv-only execution, display-session detection, clear unavailable errors, docs, tests, and Linux desktop proof.

options.title: Broader fallback stack
options.body: Support direct D-Bus or `dunstify` fallback now, accepting more code and review surface for broader desktop coverage.

options.title: Defer to companion app
options.body: Keep headless node-host notifications unsupported and let the broader Linux companion app direction own desktop notification UX later.

recommendation.title: Bounded notify-send backend
recommendation.body: Implement `notify-send` first with argv-only execution, display-session detection, clear unavailable errors, docs, tests, and Linux desktop proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and code history route this product boundary through the node-host and Linux platform work Peter has been shaping.
